newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Comdisco sees growth in electronics unit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Comdisco sees growth in electronics unit.

text.p: Comdisco Inc said a recent downturn in the semiconductor industry has had the reverse effect on its electronics group, making it one of its key growth areas for fiscal year 1997 which began this week.

Comdisco helps chip manufacturers manage their equipment costs by leasing new or refurbished equipment, among other things. As the chip industry has fallen victim to overcapacity, many manufacturers are looking for cost-effective ways to upgrade their manufacturing equipment, said executive vice president Nicholas Pontikes.

"They (semiconductor manufacturers) were bullet proof, makings billions of dollars...there were people who fooled themselves into thinking the cyclicality was dead," Pontikes said in an interview at Comdisco's headquarters. "Now with the downturn they are saying 'what is the most efficient way'."

Pontikes said Comdisco's new lease volume, or the total value of the signed contract, in its electronics group is about $400 million in fiscal 1996 -- up from $213 million the previous year and $144 million in Comdisco's fiscal 1994, when the industry was reaching its recent peak.
The semiconductor industry in general is expected to begin to bounce back in 1997, but even if it were to slip again, Comdisco sees the market remaining prime for leasing and asset management.

"Right now the percentage of manufacturers who lease is still very, very small," said Mary Moster, vice president of corporate communications for Comdisco. "So even if they didn't grow any more, the opportunity for us to grow is huge."
Pontikes said about $30 billion will be spent in 1996 on purchasing new semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and Comdisco expects more companies to lease in the future.
"Even if the industry is flat, we can grow 10 or 20 times bigger than we are right now and still have a very doable market share," he said.

Overall, the company is expected to report a greater surge in earnings than in revenues in fiscal 1996. Pontikes said he is comfortable with analysts' earnings estimates of $2.00 a share for fiscal 1996 -- about a 15 percent increase from last year's $1.73. Comdisco reported revenues of $2.24 billion in fiscal 1995.
"We made a very concerted effort to watch our expenses across the whole company," Pontikes said.

Comdisco's large-systems sector, which is essentially mainframe computers management, is not growing as rapidly as the company as a whole, and new businesses such as the network services division are still in development, also adding to the slower revenue growth, Pontikes said.
